question: Why are passengers told to keep their heads still in hyper-G?
answer: In hyper-G, the vestibular system, the balance sense in your inner ear, becomes hypersensitive to movement. The same small head turn hits it far harder and brings on motion sickness, which is why the plane is nicknamed the vomit comet. Passengers are advised to keep their heads still and look straight ahead.
